sections.content:
29,900 people

were counted on the census as "occupational therapists" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Occupational therapists work with people who have a physical or learning disability or mental illness, actively engaging them in purposeful activities in order to maximise self-confidence, independent functioning and well-being.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "occupational therapists" there were more women than men (91.2% compared with 8.8%).

This means "occupational therapists" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 8.8% and women made up 91.2% of "occupational therapists"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "occupational therapists" included:

  • legal secretaries
  • teaching assistants
  • receptionists

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "occupational therapists", 15.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "occupational therapists" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "occupational therapists" included:

  • customer service managers
  • early education and childcare services managers
  • sales accounts and business development managers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "occupational therapists", 11.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (66.7% compared with 33.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.5%) than self-employed (4.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
